title: Drainage, Recirculation and Water/Solute Mass Balance

content.overview: Water and dissolved ions enter, leave, accumulate or are taken up by the crop. Drain-to-waste and recirculating systems manage those pathways differently. Advanced management tracks volumes and concentration trends instead of assuming runoff or reservoir EC alone describes the full system.

vocabulary.definition: Drainage water leaving a root zone carrying dissolved constituents.
Collection and reuse of drainage solution after defined treatment or conditioning.
Accounting of material entering, leaving, accumulating within or being removed from a system.

sections.title: Discharge carries water and nutrients
sections.body: Drain-to-waste can control accumulation but exports water and dissolved nutrients; environmental and legal handling requirements vary by location.

sections.title: Recirculation concentrates system-history effects
sections.body: Reused solution can accumulate or deplete specific ions and can create sanitation risks if source water, return water and crop health are not monitored.

sections.title: Element-specific accumulation can hide behind acceptable growth
sections.body: Cannabis root-zone research documented substantial phosphorus accumulation at higher solution concentrations without yield benefit under the tested conditions, showing why system chemistry should be trended over time.

workedExamples: A recirculating reservoir with stable EC can still change ion ratios as the crop selectively takes up nutrients.
Large runoff volume may reduce salt concentration while increasing water/nutrient discharge costs.
commonMistakes: Treating runoff percentage as the only root-zone objective.
Assuming stable EC means stable nutrient composition.
Reusing return water without sanitation/source-risk assessment.
content.practicalApplication: Track irrigation-in volume/EC, drainage or return volume/EC, reservoir additions/replacements and periodic element-specific analyses where warranted.
content.summary: Mass-balance thinking reveals where water and ions actually go and supports more defensible drain-to-waste or recirculation decisions.
